# Whether a ball contains another, one-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_contains_ball_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Whether $Y \subseteq X$, every member of $Y$ a member of $X$, $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$; a mask that is true only if it holds:

$$m \implies Y \subseteq X.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X.contains(Y)` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `bool` | whether $X \supseteq Y$; `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $Y$, of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $m$ is true exactly when $Y \subseteq X$, every member of $Y$ a member of $X$: the answer is exact.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_contains_ball_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallPredicates.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallPredicates.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_contains_ball_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_contains_ball_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the distance of the centers and the difference of the radii as exact pairs, compared (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_contains_ball_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_contains_ball_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_sum_ord`](two_sum_ord.md), [`abs_2`](abs_2.md), [`le_2_2`](le_2_2.md).

```
# Whether a ball with a one-limb center contains another, Y inside X (milestone2.md, "One enclosure
# interface", the row of contains(Y), "Exact pairs"): |c_y - c_x| <= r_x - r_y, decided exactly as
# le_2_2(abs_2(two_sum_ord(c_y, -c_x)), two_sum_ord(r_x, -r_y)). A difference of the centers that
# overflows exceeds every radius. The special states, by the table of "The empty set and the whole
# line": the whole line contains every ball, and the empty set is in every ball; the comparison
# gives false for an empty X and a nonempty Y, and for a whole line Y in a finite X (r_x - inf is
# -inf). Exact.

ncx      = neg(cx)
(d0, d1) = two_sum_ord(cy, ncx)
(a0, a1) = abs_2(d0, d1)
nry      = neg(ry)
(g0, g1) = two_sum_ord(rx, nry)
f        = le_2_2(a0, a1, g0, g1)
wx       = eq(rx, const inf)
qy       = eq(ry, ry)
ey       = not(qy)
sp       = or(wx, ey)
m        = or(sp, f)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_contains_ball_1)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 3 domains of 3 formats | 3 420 868 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
